evidence.note: design pools knockout, overexpression and degrading antibodies in macrophages, microglia, non-human primates and an amyloid mouse model; mouse is the nearest taxon available

excluded.reason: GWAS row: rs7232-A lowers risk of AD or related dementias (OR 0.9); TREM2 is not named

statements.text: TREM2 activates the innate immune response

excluded.reason: rare coding variants in TREM2 'implicate' microglial innate immunity in AD; no direction from TREM2 to innate immunity
GWAS row: rs75932628-T (TREM2) raises AD risk (OR 2.22); innate immunity is not named

statements.text: ABI3 activates the innate immune response

excluded.reason: rare coding variants in ABI3 'implicate' microglial innate immunity in AD; no direction from ABI3 to innate immunity

mouse Abi3 S212F variant disrupts microglia and causes their loss; innate immunity is not named and the text does not say whether the variant lowers or raises ABI3 function (an 'Abi3-high state' predisposes microglia to degeneration)
GWAS row: rs616338-T (ABI3) raises AD risk (OR 1.31); innate immunity is not named

statements.text: PLCG2 activates the innate immune response

excluded.reason: rare coding variants in PLCG2 'implicate' microglial innate immunity in AD; no direction from PLCG2 to innate immunity
the hyperactive PLCG2-P522R variant is protective against AD and delays onset: PLCG2 to AD, innate immunity not named
GWAS row: rs72824905-G (PLCG2) lowers AD risk (OR 0.73); innate immunity is not named

statements.text: the innate immune response lowers the risk of Alzheimer disease

evidence.quote: the microglia-mediated innate immune response contributes directly to the development of Alzheimer's disease
evidence.note: the run's only citation for this step says innate immunity drives AD, the opposite sign; the conclusion of a case-control exome association study

statements.text: the APOE ε4 allele goes with abnormal cholesterol homeostasis
statements.sign_note: the run's polarity is 'unknown'; direction from the cited text, which says APOE4 alters cholesterol homeostasis (the target is the abnormal phenotype, so 'altered' is pos)

evidence.quote: APOE4 significantly altered signalling pathways associated with cholesterol homeostasis and transport
evidence.note: single-cell transcriptomics of post-mortem brains, APOE4 carriers against non-carriers

evidence.quote: Pharmacologically facilitating cholesterol transport increases axonal myelination and improves learning and memory in APOE4 mice
evidence.note: in vivo pharmacological perturbation in APOE4 mice; inverted: easing cholesterol transport raises myelination, so dysregulation lowers it

statements.text: myelination lowers the risk of Alzheimer disease

excluded.reason: links myelination to learning and memory in APOE4 mice ('a functional link between APOE4, cholesterol, myelination and memory'); AD itself is named only as a therapeutic opportunity
GWAS row: rs2075650-G (TOMM40 intron, author-reported APOE) raises AD risk (OR 2.53); myelination is not named

evidence.quote: the N-terminal SH2 domain of INPP5D, an important LOAD risk gene, directly interacted with the cell death regulator RIPK1 at p-Y383 to suppress RIPK1 kinase activation
evidence.note: a binding and kinase-activation result; the abstract does not name the organism of the proteins or cells

evidence.quote: Microglial INPP5D deficiency cell-autonomously promoted RIPK1-mediated transcriptional induction of diverse LOAD risk genes, proinflammatory cytokines, complements, and ROS mediators
evidence.note: the abstract never names the organism; a microglial INPP5D deletion followed through ageing to motor dysfunction is not a human experiment, so mouse is assumed

statements.text: the neuroinflammatory response raises the risk of Alzheimer disease

evidence.quote: RIPK1-mediated neuroinflammation for promoting aging-related neurodegenerative diseases, including LOAD
evidence.note: 'Our data suggest': the paper tested TDP-43 pathology, neuronal loss and motor dysfunction, not AD

excluded.reason: GWAS row: rs10933431-G (INPP5D intron) lowers AD risk (OR 0.93); neuroinflammation is not named

H1.note: one claim per gene. The mechanism calls innate immunity 'a key defense mechanism against' AD and TREM2, ABI3 and PLCG2 its drivers (neg each); MS4A4A negatively regulates TREM2 and so this defence (pos). The run never states MS4A4A's net direction in words. The chains start at the proteins; the mechanism also names TREM2 R47H, ABI3 S212F and protective PLCG2 and MS4A4A alleles, which no step uses.

H2.note: the chain's first subject is labelled 'APOE' (gene), but the title and mechanism ('APOE (specifically the APOE4 risk allele)') make it the ε4 allele, so the subject is the allele

H3.note: title: INPP5D protects against AD. The mechanism also says it slows progression and names rs10933431-G as protective; no step carries either.

findings.detail: every subject, object and context in the run has an empty curie and grounding_evidence except Alzheimer disease, although every hypothesis is marked support 'grounded'
H1 is a fan-in written as a chain: H1.2 ends at innate immunity, H1.3 starts at ABI3 and H1.4 at PLCG2; it composes as a graph, one arm per gene

the title says MS4A4A negatively regulates ABI3- and PLCG2-mediated innate immunity, but no step links MS4A4A to ABI3 or PLCG2, and the MS4A4A paper (PMID:41435829) speaks only of TREM2 (via MS4A6A and DAP12)

the only citation for 'innate immunity inhibits AD' (PMID:28714976) concludes that the innate immune response 'contributes directly to the development of Alzheimer's disease'; kept as refuting, so the H1 arms end on a refuted step
H1 lists no contradicting evidence although its own H1.5 citation states the opposite sign; no hypothesis in the run lists any

nothing the run cites says TREM2, ABI3 or PLCG2 increases innate immunity: PMID:28714976 says only that their variants 'implicate' it, PMID:42092345 reports a mouse variant that disrupts microglia, PMID:41620758 reports PLCG2 to AD
all six GWAS Catalog rows are cited for mechanistic protein or process steps they cannot state (variant to AD risk only); all excluded

PMID:41620758 says the hyperactive PLCG2-P522R variant protects against AD, a PLCG2 to AD link (gain of PLCG2 activity lowers risk) that no step makes; it was cited instead for PLCG2 to innate immunity, which it does not state
the mechanism names 'ABI3 S212F', the mouse Abi3 numbering (PMID:42092345: 'ABI3S209F (Abi3S212F in mouse)'); the human variant it cites (rs616338, PMID:28714976) is p.Ser209Phe

rs7232, presented as a protective MS4A4A allele, is a missense variant inside MS4A6A by the GWAS row's own genomic context (distance 0), with MS4A4A 12.5 kb away; the row's summary line still says 'mapped gene MS4A4A'
H2.1's subject is labelled 'APOE' (kind gene) while the title, mechanism and citation are about the APOE4 allele; curated as the ε4 allele
PMID:36385529 links myelination to learning and memory in APOE4 mice, never to AD; with the GWAS row excluded, 'myelination inhibits AD' has no support
the mechanism says the myelination route is 'completely independent of microglial inflammation or direct amyloid-beta clearance'; no cited text tests or states this

the supporting citations PMID:8346443 (APOE ε4 gene dose raises AD risk) and rs429358 (allele '?', AD age of onset, OR 3.32) state a direct APOE4 to AD link that no step makes; rs429358 cannot give a direction because the allele is unknown
rs2075650 is a TOMM40 intron variant (APOE is only the author-reported gene, 11 kb away) and is cited for 'myelination inhibits AD'

the mechanism and falsification test say INPP5D represses RIPK1 expression, but PMID:41633359 says INPP5D binds RIPK1 and suppresses its kinase activation; measuring RIPK1 expression after INPP5D knockout tests the wrong thing
'protective variants in INPP5D (such as rs10933431-G) may enhance this repression': no cited text links rs10933431 to INPP5D activity or expression, only to AD risk (OR 0.93)
PMID:41633359 tested TDP-43 pathology, neuronal loss and motor dysfunction, an ALS-like readout, and only 'suggests' its pathway promotes LOAD; kept as kind hypothesis, so H3.3 carries no weight

the supporting citations OT:INPP5D-MONDO_0004975 (association score, no direction) and CHEMBL:CHEMBL3989954 (ROSIPTOR 'targets INPP5D', phase 3, no disease or direction named) are cited by no step and state none
the RNPS1/LPIN2 abstention cites OT:RNPS1-MONDO_0004975, PMID:21283692, PMID:41865408, PMID:41205924 and PMID:39269833 and a STRING analysis, none of which is in sources.json, so it cannot be checked

every step but the last in each chain carries a structured cell_type context (microglia, oligodendrocytes) and the disease step has none; refining would cut every chain at its last step, so contexts were dropped as qualifiers; the guide's 'context limits the result' rule does not say which way to read a plain context field

no term for the APOE ε4 allele; made BLN:APOE-e4. NCIT:C105364 'Apolipoprotein E4' is in the corpus but names the protein isoform, not the allele. The only 'APOE4' label in the table is a synonym of MONDO:0007089 (Alzheimer disease 2), a grounding trap

'cholesterol dysregulation' is grounded to MP:0005278 (abnormal cholesterol homeostasis), a mouse phenotype term used for a human claim, because HP has only circulating-cholesterol concentration terms
PMID:41435829 pools macrophages, microglia, non-human primates and mice in one sentence: evidence carries one kind and one taxon, and there is no primate taxon; recorded as mechanistic, mouse
PMID:41633359's abstract never names its organism or system; there is no way to say 'non-human, organism not stated', so H3.2 is marked mouse by inference and H3.1 has no taxon
no form for a claim of independence ('completely independent of microglial inflammation'): BioLean can say X acts through Y, not that it does not

a cited text stating a direct gene to disease link (PMID:8346443 for APOE4, PMID:41620758 for PLCG2) has no home when no step makes it: a bridge would bypass the hypothesis's mechanism rather than fill a gap in it, so it is only a finding
chain composition drops disbelief: S5 is refuted by the run's own citation (d 1/2), yet the four H1 arms read belief 0 'unsupported', the same as an arm whose link merely has no evidence

all three hypotheses are rated 'low' and every arm composes with the run's own sign but is unsupported (H1: S2 to S4 empty, S5 refuted; H2: S8 empty; H3: S11 rests on a 'suggest' sentence); the low ratings are apt
NCIT terms are in the corpus (NCIT:C105364 Apolipoprotein E4) but neither the guide prefix table nor render.py PREFIX_KIND covers NCIT, so a curator cannot tell whether one may be used
PMID:41620758 also reports that APOE ε4 carriers with TREM2-R62H have an earlier AD onset, a TREM2 to AD link no step makes
